summary: All seven minors from M3's review round 5 were checked against the live tree and applied. No rule and no value changed: nothing re-blessed, goldens and digest untouched. Tests: three new assertions catch V1's seven surviving mutants (V2's fprobereach is V1's R5p1). The Edge.spec ones kill R5p1 and R5h1. In Factors.spec the union chord's case kills R5c3 and the ties R5c1, R5c2, R5c6 and R5c7. Each new assertion passes on the tree and fails only on its own mutant (mut/mutants.py). The case count is unchanged at 749, with T-PERF-01 the 614th, so the stale counts become 613 of 749 in §4.9, §14.11 and Perf.spec. O10's lean closure cost now reads × 1.00–1.17, about 59–64 ms, and the accept column says a tenth to a sixth of the slowest design's time. Fixer G's form is widened to × 1.02–1.24 from V2's own runs. V1's shift finding reproduces byte for byte (Z −0.037: G moves on 2,081 of 10,883 designs, 11 tiers; Y +0.3317: 357 designs, 2 tiers), but V1's second mechanism was wrong. Most Z moves are not hide-test ties: they come from M2's measure rank, which keys on |z| among parts of one volume, y and x. A Z shift reorders those parts, and the sub-grid budget, spent in rank order, runs out at other patches. With the rank keyed on z alone, a scratch variant, only 110 designs and 2 tiers move. So O11 (j), §5's promise, §5.6, §0.5, §4.4 and §17.2 state that, marked [Decision to confirm] (O11). The flush-rib class is named O11 (k) with V1's figures, which reproduce line for line, at §4.6 row 1, §5's promise, §5.6 and §0.5. O11's (iii) ranges and question now read (a)–(k), and the Edge and Factors headers gained comment-only notes. M3-notes has a "Fix round 5, the minors' fixer" section, and E-S2.13 has a fix round 5 bullet plus V2's timing in the mouth bullet. The final scripts/verify is GREEN: 749/0/0, exit 0, at 0–37 % busy, T-PERF-01 worst valid 9 at 57.55 ms. Nothing committed; docs.rar untouched.

deviations: V1's issue 3 (shift on the plausible set): the figures hold, but V1's second mechanism does not. V1 named 'a face on the hide test's boundary (§17.2's ties)'. The measured cause of the fuller's move, and of about 1,971 of the 2,081 Z moves and 9 of the 11 tiers, is M2's measure rank keyed on |z|, which reorders parts of one volume, y and x, together with the sub-grid budget spent in that order. This is shown by subwork, explog, rankcmp and czrank. So O11 (j), §5's promise, §5.6, §0.5, §17.2 and §4.4 state that instead of V1's text. The rule itself is unchanged.
O10: fixer G's end-test range is widened to × 1.02–1.24, because V2's own runs reach × 1.2366 on worst valid 9. V2's proposed text changed only the lean range.
O11 (k): I added which shift carries it. Z shifts do; no Y shift moved it, even with the design turned 2° about X (flushtilt). Everything else matches V1's text.
V1's and V2's R5p1 tests are the same call, so they went in as one assertion.
V1's R5h1 block uses the case's own g (0.01200005) for its lower face. V1 wrote HIDE_OFFSET + 0.5·EPS_GEOM, the same gap.
V1's tie fixture uses new local names (under/pa/pb/qa/qb/over). V1's r and p1 would have shadowed locals declared later in the same case.

Beyond the proposed texts: §4.4's rank paragraph, §14.6 T-EDG-01, §17.2's S2 invisible-construction row, the Edge.luau and Factors.luau header comments for (k), and **[Decision to confirm]** (§17.1 O11 (j)/(k)) marks at §4.4 and §4.6.
One Factors.luau comment was reworded after the first green verify. A second full verify was then run as the final one.
openIssues: For the lead (O11 (j)): most of the Z-shift class is M2's measure rank, which keys on |cz|, not rounding. On a third of the plausible set, a 0.037 Z shift moves G on 2,081 designs and changes a tier on 11. Ranking by z alone (scratch czrank) would leave 110 designs and 2 tiers, and as built it reads only 6 of these designs differently, with no tier change. That would change an M2 rule. The verdict's rank (Sampling.ranked) has the same |z| key. So it is only stated, under **[Decision to confirm]** (§17.1 O11), with the default as built. Its effect on the fixtures' goldens and on S-PAR-02's digest was not measured.

T-PERF-01 passed in both of my verify runs: worst valid 9 at 57.55 ms (0–37 % busy) and 57.41 ms (3–31 %), against the 60 ms guard. The lead's quiet verify and S-PAR-02's three Studio Play sessions (the digest is unchanged since fix round 2) are still pending before the commit.
O10's closure timings for review round 5 are V2's runs, read but not re-measured by me.
